facts.label: Used to
facts.sub: Use used to + verbo base para algo do passado que mudou. No negativo e na pergunta use use to: I didn’t use to like it. Did you use to eat it?

facts.label: Costumava / Antes…
facts.sub: Use used to + verbo base para falar de hábito ou gosto do passado que não existe mais: I used to hate vegetables. Funciona com todas as pessoas. Não muda com he/she.

facts.label: Não costumava
facts.sub: No negativo, use didn’t use to, sem o d: I didn’t use to like peas. O did já marca o passado. Em frases afirmativas, o d fica: I used to.

items.s: Used to is for past habits.
We say I didn’t used to like it.
items.why: We say I didn’t use to like it.

items.s: I used to hate vegetables means I hate them now.
items.why: It means I do not hate them now.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Used to is for past habits. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say I didn’t used to like it. → Falso (We say I didn’t use to like it.)
I used to hate vegetables means I hate them now. → Falso (It means I do not hate them now.)

pages.title: A green restaurant in Portland · 1/3
paragraphs: Al and Rui are old friends in Portland. They meet for lunch at a small green café. The menu has many vegetable dishes. Rui looks at the salad with a smile. Years ago, his plate looked very different. Now the two men talk about change.
“Rui, you’re eating salad! You used to hate vegetables.” says Al. “I know. I used to push them to the side of my plate.” says Rui. “Did you use to eat anything green as a child?” says Al.
